descriptionChirho: The indeclinable proper noun Ἱερουσαλήμ (the Semitic/Hebrew form of 'Jerusalem'), referring to the holy city of Jerusalem, capital of Judea and site of the Temple. This is a single referent, not polysemous. Uniformly rendered Ger. 'Jerusalem,' Fr. 'Jérusalem,' Heb. 'יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,' Spa. 'Jerusalén/Ierousalēm,' Arb. 'أُورُشَلِيمَ,' Kor. '예루살렘,' Hin. 'यरूशलेम.' The four auto-clusters (69433, 69434, 69435, 69436) are split only on minor transliteration differences (Ierousalēm vs. Ierousalem, with/without 'of') and different grammatical cases in surrounding context (genitive 'of Jerusalem,' dative 'in Jerusalem,' accusative 'to Jerusalem,' vocative 'O Jerusalem'). As an indeclinable noun, the form never changes; it is always Ἱερουσαλήμ. All 76 occurrences refer to the same city. Contexts include: the Gospels (Matt 23:37, Luke 2:25/41/43/45, 4:9, 9:31/51/53, 10:30, 13:4/33/34), Acts, Romans 15, and Revelation 3:12.
